# lilBunnyRabbit — brand & theme

> A two-mode colour system generated from one seed, plus the mark, the type and the rules for
> using them. Take what you need. Guide: https://lilbunnyrabbit.github.io/brand/

Everything below is the whole system. If you are answering a question about these colours, or
generating code that uses them, this file is enough — you do not need to scrape the page.

The palette is authored in [Chromatics](https://lilbunnyrabbit.github.io/chromatics/), stored in
OKLCH, and shipped as hex. Source of truth for the values:
`src/lib/brand/config/palette.dark.ts` and `palette.light.ts` in
https://github.com/lilBunnyRabbit/brand.

## The two modes

**Dark is the brand. Light is product UI only.** Marketing, social cards, the app icon and
anything doing brand recognition are always dark. Light exists so a product surface can render
light; it is not an identity palette and it is not a second brand.

Both modes carry **the same 17 token keys**. Nothing rebinds between them — switching mode is a
scope change, not a remapping. In CSS that is `[data-theme='light']` on any element; dark sits on
`:root`, so the canonical mode needs no attribute and no JavaScript.

```css
:root, [data-theme='dark'] { /* the 17 --brand-* values, dark */ }
[data-theme='light']       { /* the same 17 keys, light values */ }
```

Every token is a custom property named `--brand-<key>`, e.g. `--brand-primary`,
`--brand-background_lightest`.

## Dark — the brand palette

All 17 derived from one literal, the seed `oklch(0.255 0.0233 230.47)`. Nothing is hand-picked.

| token | hex | oklch | what it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `background_lightest` | `#2a3f4a` | `oklch(0.355 0.03244 230.47)` | surface ladder, +span |
| `background_lighter` | `#233640` | `oklch(0.3217 0.02939 230.47)` | +2/3 span |
| `background_light` | `#1d2d36` | `oklch(0.2883 0.02635 230.47)` | +1/3 span |
| `background` | `#17252c` | `oklch(0.255 0.0233 230.47)` | **the seed** — the page |
| `background_dark` | `#111d23` | `oklch(0.2217 0.02025 230.47)` | −1/3 span |
| `background_darker` | `#0b151a` | `oklch(0.1883 0.01721 230.47)` | −2/3 span |
| `background_darkest` | `#060d11` | `oklch(0.155 0.01416 230.47)` | −span |
| `foreground` | `#b1aba8` | `oklch(0.745 0.00777 50.47)` | all body copy |
| `tertiary` | `#baa7ab` | `oklch(0.745 0.0233 2.47)` | brand, rank 1 |
| `secondary` | `#b2a6c5` | `oklch(0.745 0.0466 302.47)` | brand, rank 2 |
| `primary` | `#a4b483` | `oklch(0.745 0.0699 122.47)` | brand, rank 3 |
| `accent` | `#dc9b76` | `oklch(0.745 0.0932 50.47)` | brand, rank 4 |
| `cottontail` | `#e0f9ab` | `oklch(0.945 0.10332 122.47)` | identity — badge ink only |
| `success` | `#7ac26a` | `oklch(0.745 0.1398 140)` | state |
| `warning` | `#e49b39` | `oklch(0.745 0.1398 70)` | state |
| `error` | `#f88876` | `oklch(0.745 0.1398 30)` | state |
| `info` | `#49b7fb` | `oklch(0.745 0.1398 240)` | state |

The ladder is symmetric, ±0.1 lightness, chroma proportional to lightness so lighter shades read
as elevated. Hue is identity and chroma is rank: the seed's chroma `c` is the quantum and every
brand rank is an integer multiple of it (1c, 2c, 3c, 4c), with states at 6c. 5c is deliberately
empty so the brand band and the state band stay apart.

## Light — the product UI twin

Same keys, same jobs. Authored as resolved literals rather than arithmetic, because two of them
come out of a contrast solver and two out of a gamut mapper.

| token (`light_*` in the scheme) | hex | oklch |
|---|---|---|
| `background_lightest` | `#fff5e6` | `oklch(0.9744 0.023 80)` |
| `background_lighter` | `#fcf2e2` | `oklch(0.9646 0.023 80)` |
| `background_light` | `#f8efdf` | `oklch(0.9548 0.023 80)` |
| `background` | `#f5ecdc` | `oklch(0.945 0.023 80)` — the page |
| `background_dark` | `#e8decf` | `oklch(0.905 0.023 80)` |
| `background_darker` | `#dbd1c2` | `oklch(0.865 0.023 80)` |
| `background_darkest` | `#cec4b5` | `oklch(0.825 0.023 80)` |
| `foreground` | `#474f5c` | `oklch(0.425 0.0233 260)` |
| `tertiary` | `#4e4d59` | `oklch(0.425 0.0205 290.47)` |
| `secondary` | `#335653` | `oklch(0.425 0.0409 190)` |
| `primary` | `#6a442f` | `oklch(0.425 0.0614 50.47)` |
| `accent` | `#6b3c5e` | `oklch(0.425 0.0818 338.47)` |
| `cottontail` | `#af5100` | `oklch(0.545 0.1431 50.47)` |
| `success` | `#225e12` | `oklch(0.425 0.1228 140)` |
| `warning` | `#535200` | `oklch(0.4268 0.0928 109.31)` |
| `error` | `#852d22` | `oklch(0.425 0.1228 30)` |
| `info` | `#00548a` | `oklch(0.4329 0.1119 246.24)` |

Three things about light that are easy to get wrong:

- **The light primary is orange, not green.** Dark's green sits 13.1 ΔE from its own darkened form
  on this ground — it reads as a shade of the paper rather than a colour on it. Orange measures
  15.2 in the same position. Light is fitted to its own ground, it does not inherit dark's wheel.
- **`cottontail` changes job.** In dark it is the badge ink. In light it is a UI colour — focus
  ring, marker, chart highlight. Never text (3.04–4.86 across the shades), never the logo.
- **The ladder is asymmetric**: 0.0294 up, 0.120 down. Up is limited by the gamut, not by
  contrast — past L 0.9744 the page tint no longer fits in sRGB. `background_lightest` is
  `#fff5e6`, a cream. **It is not white and must not be "corrected" to white** — at L 1.0 the sRGB
  chroma ceiling is zero, which strips the tint and puts a hole in the ladder.

## One fixed colour

`mark_ears` `#e0f9ab` `oklch(0.945 0.1033 122.47)` — the mark's pale ears. Byte-identical in both
modes, belongs to neither palette. Only the disc themes. Deriving light ears from `light_primary`
gives 2.28 on the disc against 7.36 for this, and they vanish under greyscale.

## The contrast contract

Every one of the 9 rail colours (`foreground`, the 4 brand, the 4 states) clears **WCAG AA 4.5:1
against every one of the 7 shades** — 63 pairs per mode, both modes.

- dark: 63/63, worst **4.587** (`error` on `background_lightest`)
- light: 63/63, worst **4.591** (`success` on `background_darkest`)

The practical consequence: **any shade can back any section and nothing needs re-checking.**
`cottontail` is excluded — it is an identity colour and makes no contract claim.

`tests/palette.test.ts` asserts the contract, so it cannot rot silently.

## Modifiers — opacity, never a new colour

Interaction and de-emphasis are alpha on an existing colour. Composited in gamma sRGB
(`color-mix(in srgb, …)`), which is what a browser actually paints.

| name | alpha | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `hover` | 0.85 | |
| `active` | 0.70 | |
| `muted` | 0.65 | AA-large at best — captions and metadata only, not on the lightest two shades |
| `disabled` | 0.38 | 2.17:1. Legally exempt, never for anything informational |
| `border` | 0.67 | the lowest alpha clearing 3:1 on **every** shade |

Available pre-composited as `--fg-muted`, `--fg-disabled`, `--fg-border`, and as `--alpha-*`.

## Rules

Hard don'ts:

1. **Light mode is UI only.** Never for brand recognition, marketing, the app icon or social cards.
2. **Nothing brand-coloured on white.** The light ground is `#f5ecdc`, a cream. On actual white the
   dark brand colours vanish — primary is 2.23:1, cottontail 1.15:1. Light mode is not permission
   to use `#fff`.
3. **No two brand colours adjacent or layered.** They are all the same lightness, so side by side
   they blur into one shape. A gap or a border fixes it.
4. **No gradients between brand colours.** Same lightness means the gradient has nowhere to travel
   and comes out muddy. Between two shades is fine.
5. **No white text on a brand fill.** White on primary is 2.23:1. Use `#17252c` and you get
   6.55–7.06.
6. **Do not add colours.** Whatever seems to be missing is either a shade or an existing colour
   turned down.
7. **Do not re-tint the greys.** The backgrounds are blue and the brand is green on purpose.
8. **Do not "fix" the logo's contrast.** The bright badge is 1.94:1 deliberately. Logos are exempt
   (WCAG 1.4.3, 1.4.11). No stroke, no shadow, no lighter green.

Take care:

- **No more than three shades per viewport.** Neighbours are ~1.1:1 apart, so a fourth stops
  reading as structure.
- **Muted text is for captions, not content.** At 65% it is 3.76:1 on the page and 2.96 on the
  lightest shade.

## Typography

| face | CSS var | role | weights | licence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inter | `--font-sans` | everything you read — headings, body, labels | 400 500 600 700 800 | SIL OFL 1.1 |
| Hack | `--font-mono` | every value: hexes, formulas, ratios, token names. And the wordmark | 400 700 | MIT (+ Bitstream Vera) |

Both self-hosted. There is no published size ladder — `--text-*` exists in the stylesheet but the
steps are an implementation detail, not a brand rule.

## Getting the palette

The guide offers the whole thing in four formats, both modes in each, with the derivation formula
per colour:

- **CSS** custom properties — `palette.css`
- **Tailwind v4** `@theme` — `palette.theme.css`, usable as `bg-background`, `text-primary`, …
- **JSON** — `palette.json`, hex + oklch + rgb + formula per token
- **Markdown** — `palette.md`

All four are on https://lilbunnyrabbit.github.io/brand/#assets, along with the logo SVGs.
